subject.name: delulu-1.0.0.dwx
subject._note: Filled at the release cut (2026-07-20) from the actual artifact: release-artifacts/1.0.0/delulu-1.0.0.dwx, built twice and byte-identical, signed (detached ed25519, key 5c3a457a92fe50f2...), verified before this digest was written. SHA256SUMS ships beside the artifact.

internalParameters.SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH: not set — deliberately: the artifact embeds no timestamps by construction, and byte-identity across independent builds is witnessed without it (criterion4_a_dwx_artifact_is_byte_identical_across_builds, and re-verified at the cut)

builder._honesty: This build ran on a developer machine, not on hosted CI with an attested identity. Saying so is the point: the value of provenance is that it describes the build truthfully, and a statement claiming a builder identity it does not have is a supply-chain lie with a schema around it.

predicate._slsaNote: SLSA L3 requires a hosted, attested build service; this repository is not publicly hosted, so L3 is not achieved and is not claimed. What IS achieved and independently checkable: a pinned toolchain, vendored dependencies, and byte-identical artifacts across independent builds (build-order D6, witnessed by criterion4_a_dwx_artifact_is_byte_identical_across_builds). Reproducibility is the property that actually lets someone else verify the artifact; the attestation level is how a third party learns it without rebuilding. We have the first and not yet the second, and this field says which.
predicate._signature: Release artifacts carry detached ed25519 signatures (<artifact>.sig), verifiable with `delulu verify-sig`. Signing authenticates ORIGIN, not behavior — what the artifact can do is the authority report, and that is recomputed rather than trusted.
